description: Per-shot pixel tolerances for parity specs, measured as run-to-run noise of the live oracle (same Mac, Chromium build in capture-meta.json). Canvas PNGs and shot JSON (gl draw calls/triangles, html, cssHash, storage) were exact in every run: tolerance 0. Only DOM-overlay PNGs show noise.

runs.liveVsLive: capture-live-baselines.mjs --verify (fresh capture vs committed live baselines)
runs.localVsLive: capture-live-baselines.mjs --origin local / npm run test:parity (dist/ served under the live origin + window.__parity), 2026-10-19: canvas, shot JSON, traces and oracle scene dumps exact in every run
runs.localVsLocalR186: phase 10 (three 0.186.1, retuned lighting): npm run parity:baselines, then capture-live-baselines.mjs --origin local + npm run test:parity, 2026-10-19: canvas PNGs, shot JSON, traces and scene dumps exact; DOM noise only on shots already listed, all within their existing tolerance/ceiling (none widened)
runs.localVsLocalPhase12: phase 12 (IndexedDB store, learning quiz, save-code buttons): npm run parity:baselines, then npm run test:parity: canvas PNGs, shot JSON, traces and scene dumps exact; one new DOM-noise shot (mobile milo-dialog, 2 px)
runs.localVsLocalPhase19: phases 14/15/19 merge (field, forest, shop): npm run parity:baselines, then npm run test:parity: canvas PNGs, shot JSON, traces and scene dumps exact; one new DOM-noise shot (mobile quiz-hint-1, 221 px, two-state raster)

policy.rule: shot tolerance = max observed ratio x2, rounded up to 1e-4; shots not listed use 0
policy.structuralCeiling: nonDeterministic shots pass on pixels up to shot.structuralCeiling (default domPngCeiling) only when their shot JSON is byte-exact

recommendation: Keep pixel gating for canvas shots (exact) and for DOM shots at tolerance 0. For the listed shots, do not raise global tolerance: either mask the off-screen world labels (#tower-label, #city-label when their translate x exceeds the viewport) in DOM shots, or gate them structurally via the shot JSON (html + cssHash + gl calls/triangles are exact) and the oracle scene JSON. Structural gating is preferred because it is exact and catches label text/position regressions that a mask would hide.
